propositions: RemoteRef is defined as a frozen value type but never constructed in production code, so its instance field is intentional documentation rather than observed behaviour.
A remote_ref() member is declared on the Backend Protocol and implemented on both concrete backends, returning a RemoteRef whose instance is injected at construction by the build_backend factories.

The instance value is derived by a pure helper that normalises the configured base URL so equivalent spellings (trailing slash, host case, default port, scheme, context path) agree while different deployments differ.
remote_ref() must not resolve settings at call time; injecting instance via the constructor avoids breaking contract tests built without ambient config and avoids a Protocol isinstance regression.

Populating instance does NOT prevent local-id collision between same-vendor deployments because _jira_key_to_local_id derives the id from the Jira key alone, and vendor already separates Cloud from DC.
Both ADRs (0055 and 0035) and the RemoteRef docstring are amended to correct the collision claim, and a regression test pins the known local-id limitation as deliberately unfixed.
